name: turning the jacket
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Turning the jacket is an Irish folkloric symbol. The traveler turns the garment backward or inside out. This act is a sure protection against fairies. Iron and salt serve the same purpose. Without this guard, fairies might kidnap the traveler away.

okr.objective: Record the Irish folkloric symbol of turning the jacket.
key_results: The traveler turns the garment backward or inside out
The act guards against fairies who might kidnap the traveler
Like iron and salt, it gives sure protection
